correctness.rationale: For nonempty ordered rung columns, each consecutive pair forces a rail cut in its gap; edge count permits exactly one there and no others. Conversely, the uncut rail in each gap connects the bounding rungs, and both portions of the cut rail reach a bounding rung; tails are intact. Thus the multiplicity is the product of twice each gap length. Summing over the two boundary offsets and positive gaps gives 2^(k−1) binom(n+k−1,2k−1). At c=t/n² the masses multiplied by n tend to 2^(k−1)t^k/(2k−1)!, dominated by 2^(3k−2)t^k/(2k−1)!. Normalization yields the stated odd-Poisson, total variation convergence, pgf and mean. The conditional position weights give the product-of-gaps density by midpoint Riemann sums, normalized by the Dirichlet integral. Independent uniform discrete cuts in each gap couple to independent uniform continuum cut positions, with independent fair rail labels. Equivalently, conditional on k, the ordered unlabelled rungs and cuts alternate as 2k−1 uniform order statistics. The antisymmetric rail sector gives the weighted rung kernel 2c(L+2cI)^−1. Its normalized midpoint cosine modes give the stated Neumann kernel: after step embedding the bounded mode functions converge for fixed m and the summable O(m^−2) bound controls the kernel tails uniformly. The Fredholm series for the step-kernel process therefore converges to that for the limiting kernel; rounding points in the cells to their midpoints shifts positions by at most 1/n. The count eigenvalues give the two sharp-scale ends by a vanishing nonconstant-mode sum or by any fixed number of modes tending to certainty, respectively. Independent edge-subset checks at n≤6 agree with all rung-set multiplicities.
residual_risks: The finite checks do not prove a limit; the analytic summable bound and conditional spatial argument are essential. The submitted verification script was not replayed.
